problem: VLMs process 360° panoramas as flat ERP images, ignoring spherical geometry, so predicted target directions suffer seam discontinuities, latitude distortion and interpolation drift, and are inconsistent under agent rotation/motion.
motivation: Map-free navigation and active visual search need a continuous egocentric target direction that stays consistent as the agent moves. Per-frame pixel-coordinate prediction from VLMs is noisy, discards uncertainty and drifts under camera rotation, so a geometry-respecting state representation is needed.
key_idea: Treat VLM target-response maps as directional log-likelihoods lifted onto the sphere and accumulate them with a recursive Bayesian filter whose belief is stored in spherical-harmonic coefficients (SH-BF), propagated exactly by Wigner-D rotations.
insight: Decoupling semantic perception (frozen VLM) from geometric state estimation lets small backbones beat larger ones (Qwen2.5-VL-7B+EAGOR 40.10 on HOS vs Gemma-3-12B 25.67; 25.2 vs 72B 18.1 on OSR-Bench). Baselines with only seam fix (Cent-Circ) or only temporal accumulation (Grid) fail (SR 62 and 82 with worse SPL), showing that both spherical geometry and equivariant propagation are needed. The SH bandlimit ablation shows L=7 trades resolution (~25°) against Gibbs ringing.
method: VLM evidence extraction: frozen VLM produces a target-conditioned response map over the ERP panorama, normalized to [0,1] and treated as observation likelihood
Spherical lifting: pixels are mapped to unit directions on S^2 (azimuth/elevation), giving a directional likelihood, converted to log-likelihood r_t=log(l_t+eps)
SH-BF representation: belief f_t stored as real SH coefficients with bandlimit L=7 (64 coefficients, ~25° resolution); observation projected onto SH basis with cos(phi) area element
Rotation propagation: previous posterior coefficients rotated into the current viewer frame via Wigner-D matrices (exact, no resampling); for planar navigation reduces to yaw change
Translation propagation: first-order advection along the FOE/FOC flow direction with a Lie-derivative operator, scaled by ||t||/rho_min; applied only when occluded/no fresh observation
Belief update: log-space Bayesian update by adding coefficients c_t = c~_t + b_t (first frame initializes posterior)
Direction decoding: first moment of the log-belief, m_t/||m_t||, computed in O(1) from degree-1 coefficients; its norm serves as a confidence

setting.backbone: Frozen Qwen2.5-VL (3B, 7B) and Gemma-3 (4B, 12B) VLMs, plus analytic SH belief filter
setting.action_space: move fixed step along predicted egocentric direction (continuous heading)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D); HOS and OSR-Bench datasets; real Unitree Go2

numbers_note: Real-world results only qualitative (figures). Simulation benchmarks are custom Habitat setups, not standard VLN/ObjectNav.
results: EAGOR improves frozen VLMs on HOS (Qwen2.5-VL-7B 27.24→40.10) and OSR-Bench (16.8→25.2, beating Qwen2.5-VL-72B at 18.1). In map-free Habitat navigation it reaches 94% SR, 56.8 SPL, 50.2 steps and 33.8° MAE versus Centroid's 82 SR, 54.4 SPL, 61.0 steps, 45.9° MAE; temporal inconsistency drops to 2.6°/step.
limitations: Depends on VLM semantic evidence; fails on rare targets, OCR/fine text, multi-instance confusion and false detections (overall HOS success 40.1%)
Translation/parallax handled only approximately (worst-case bound, fixed step); range-unaware
Extra inference time (~1.6s vs ~1.0s); bandlimit L=7 limits angular resolution to ~25°; evaluation on custom sim tasks, real-world only qualitative
